swe1_cover.text: Cover (only what the GPIO scope names, for the instance GPIOA; name the registers GPIO_<REG> as the RM0486 GPIOx_ registers of the instance): ST's classic HAL GPIO driver as delivered (STM32CubeN6 v1.4.0), used as is (FROZEN), for port A (GPIOA); Pin configuration: input, output push-pull/open-drain, alternate function and analog modes, output speed, pull-up/pull-down and alternate function selection of the selected pins; Pin data: read a pin, set or reset a pin, toggle pins, set and reset several pins at once; the pin configuration lock; Out of scope: external interrupt/event modes and callbacks, pin de-initialisation, retime/delay settings, secure/privilege attributes, other ports

swe1_effect_rule.text: Use op "write" with "value" (an integer or "0x..." string) for a field the requirement writes a value to, op "set"/"clear" for a single bit; a function that writes a caller-supplied value gets one entry with a representative value and the api_calls args pass that value. Read and query functions get op no_write with register/field.

target_model.text: The simulated GPIOA (factory/sim/stm32n6/gpio_model.py): Behavioural GPIOA model (RM0486 rev 4 chapter 15, feature 015) with the port A reset values: GPIO_MODER (0x00) 0xABFFEFFF, GPIO_OSPEEDR (0x08) 0x0C000000, GPIO_PUPDR (0x0C) 0x64000000, GPIO_SECCFGR (0x30) and GPIO_PRIVCFGR (0x34) 0x0000FFFF (F016 model gate: RM0486 reset values), the others 0. GPIO_BSRR (0x18, write-only) sets the GPIO_ODR (0x14) bits of BSy (bits 15:0) and clears those of BRy (bits 31:16), BSy winning when both are set; GPIO_BRR (0x28, write-only) clears GPIO_ODR bits. GPIO_IDR (0x10, read-only) reads GPIO_ODR back for pins in output (MODEy = 01) or alternate function (10) mode, 1 for input pins (00) with pull-up (PUPDy = 01) and 0 otherwise (pull-down, floating, analog). GPIO_OTYPER (0x04), GPIO_AFRL (0x20) and GPIO_AFRH (0x24) are storage. The lock sequence (GPIO_LCKR 0x1C), TrustZone, delay and advanced configuration registers are out of the work orders' scope: storage, not modelled. Expected values in target checks follow this model.

hal_api.text: Interfaces (the delivered ST HAL API exactly as declared in software/hal/stm32n6xx_hal_gpio.h and stm32n6xx_hal_gpio_ex.h: void HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, const GPIO_InitTypeDef *GPIO_Init); GPIO_PinState HAL_GPIO_ReadPin(const GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, uint16_t GPIO_Pin); void HAL_GPIO_WritePin(GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, uint16_t GPIO_Pin, GPIO_PinState PinState); void HAL_GPIO_TogglePin(GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, uint16_t GPIO_Pin); void HAL_GPIO_WriteMultipleStatePin(GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, uint16_t PinReset, uint16_t PinSet); HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_GPIO_LockPin(GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx, uint16_t GPIO_Pin); the functions take the instance pointer GPIO_TypeDef *GPIOx (the CMSIS device structure GPIOA) and GPIO_InitTypeDef (Pin, Mode, Pull, Speed, Alternate) - describe what the delivered declarations are, never a different API)

hal_args_example.text: , e.g. "GPIOA" and "&(GPIO_InitTypeDef){ .Pin = <a constant of stm32n6xx_hal_gpio.h>, ... }" (the instance is ALWAYS GPIOA; a configuration is a compound literal with the fields the case needs: the gates bind them to the delivered code); invalid cases pass the invalid value (NULL, an out-of-range constant)

hal_contract_rule.text: HAL_GPIO_Init with a valid configuration gets op write entries for every GPIO register field it writes for that configuration (the configured or default values), status HAL_OK; an invalid configuration or NULL argument gets op no_write without register/field and status HAL_ERROR; query functions get op no_write. Every case id is unique UPPER_CASE. Never add an entry the requirement text does not state.

hal_failure_responses.text: one requirement per failure response of the scope: an invalid parameter -> no register access; an invalid configuration value -> HAL_ERROR without writing the register it configures; a busy handle -> HAL_BUSY where the delivered API declares it; and one timing requirement: no HAL_GPIO_ function waits on a GPIO flag
